name: Imsterberg
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village above Imst with an authentic charm and a breathtaking view of the Ötztaler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Imsterberg is situated at an elevation of 879 metres in the Tyrolean Upper Inn Valley within the district of Imst, beautifully perched on a sun-drenched mountain terrace south of the River Inn. The municipal area spans just under eleven square kilometres and is home to around 840 inhabitants. Positioned directly opposite the district capital of Imst, the village commands an astonishing 180-degree panoramic vista across the Inn Valley, the Gurgl Valley entrance, and the rugged limestone walls of the Lechtal Alps crowned by Mount Muttekopf. Imsterberg is characterized by traditional rural hamlets including Ried, Endsfeld, Höfle, and Spadegg along the slopes, alongside Imsterau on the valley floor. Far removed from mass tourism, it provides an authentic haven for nature lovers and hikers.

History

The earliest documented record of Imsterberg dates to around 1300/1310 in the land registries of the powerful Starkenberg noble family, noting early clearing settlements named Awe, Spadegg, and Ried. For centuries, rural life centred on subsistence alpine pasture farming and forestry under the dominion of the knights of Starkenberg, whose ancestral seat at Kronburg Castle overlooks the nearby cliffs. In 1811, Imsterberg attained the status of an independent political municipality. The hamlet of Endsfeld houses the late-Baroque Parish Church of the Seven Sorrows of Mary, tracing its roots to 1390. Erected in 1791, the church preserves a fine Gothic Pietà dating to the early 15th century alongside exquisite sculptures by Baroque woodcarver Johann Schnegg.

Getting There

Reaching Imsterberg is remarkably straightforward. By automobile, motorists exit the Inntal Motorway A12 at the Imst-Au junction, crossing the bridge over the River Inn into Imsterau. From there, a well-maintained, scenic alpine road winds upward through sweeping curves to the village centre in roughly five minutes. Train passengers benefit from the local Imsterberg railway stop on the valley floor along the Arlberg Railway line, served by Tyrol S-Bahn lines S4 and S5 as well as regional trains. Alternatively, the intercity express station Imst-Pitztal lies only five kilometres away, connected by local VVT bus links.

Tips

One of the most rewarding excursions leads from Imsterberg down through the dramatic Kronburg Gorge (Kronburger Tobel)—plunging up to 70 metres deep—towards the ruined medieval fortress of Kronburg and its welcoming monastery guesthouse. Hikers and mountain bikers ascend to the Imsterberger Venetalm hut at nearly 2,000 metres altitude, cherished for hearty Tyrolean alpine delicacies and sweeping vistas across the Tschirgant range. From the hut, high-altitude trails lead toward the Glanderspitze and the Venet massif. Down on the valley floor, the level Inn Cycle Path offers relaxed cycling, while winter brings family skiing at nearby Mount Venet.
